title: Choose a Gaussian mixture
description: You fit Gaussian mixtures and select their component count with BIC.

steps.description: You start each fit with sampled means, shared initial covariance estimates, and equal component weights. The outer loop tries five initializations by default.
You normalize the component scores into gamma, each point's component responsibilities. The loop stops when successive log likelihoods differ by less than tol.
You use gamma to update weights, means, and covariances, then retain the fit with the highest log likelihood. BIC adds a parameter-count penalty to negative twice the log likelihood.
You fit one through five components and save each model beside its BIC value.

steps.question: Which component count does the recorded output select, even though log likelihood keeps increasing?
steps.answer: It selects three components. Their BIC, 3289.20, is the lowest recorded value.

steps.description: You plot the selected mixture density with the observations and component means. The second plot compares BIC across the five component counts.
